item.title: 2Flow2SN: Dusty Supernova Cosmology with Photometric Redshifts and Contamination using Neural Simulation-Based Inference
item.description: arXiv:2610.30244v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photometric Type Ia supernova (SN Ia) cosmology in the era of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) demands statistical frameworks that simultaneously account for selection effects, photometric redshift uncertainties and non-Ia contamination at scale. We present FlowSN2, a modular statistical framework combining hierarchical Bayesian modelling and simulation-based inference (SBI), that reframes photometric SN cosmology from a regression task to a joint inference problem over light curve summaries and photometric redshifts. By employing neural likelihood estimation via normalising flows, FlowSN2 approximates the data distributions of selected objects in a form that can be reused across different cosmological models, achieving amortisation over the Hubble diagram. This amortisation enables inference across alternative cosmological parameterisations, such as $w_0w_a\mathrm{CDM}$, away from the fiducial training cosmology. The framework integrates a standardisation model that disentangles intrinsic SN variations from extrinsic host-galaxy dust effects and adopts a principled Bayesian resampling approach to propagate SN classification uncertainty, without requiring an explicit contaminant likelihood. Across simulated tests spanning five cosmological parameter sets, our framework recovers true cosmological and population parameters, with posteriors in close agreement with both tractable analytical solutions and pure-Ia baselines. Conveniently, the framework enables Bayesian model comparison at negligible additional computational cost, providing a valuable tool for addressing debates surrounding SN standardisation and evolving dark energy. Capable of scaling to over a hundred thousand SNe without retraining, FlowSN2 offers an interpretable and statistically principled solution for cosmological inference with upcoming wide-field photometric surveys.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin M. Boyd, Maximilian Autenrieth, Kaisey S. Mandel, Matthew Grayling, Madeleine Ginolin, Lisa Kelsey, Stephen Thorp

item.title: Density-split analyses of the pairwise kinetic Sunyaev-Zeldovich effect
item.description: arXiv:2610.30267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the dependence of the kinetic Sunyaev-Zeldovich (kSZ) effect on the environments of foreground cosmological structures. Standard pairwise kSZ estimators exploit the fact that galaxies below separations of $\sim 200\,h^{-1}{\rm M}_\odot$ fall towards each other on average, yielding a negative mean pairwise kSZ signal. However, this signal is the residual from a near-cancellation between outflows from underdense regions and infall towards overdensities giving a large variance in the pairwise velocity distribution and hence a low signal-to-noise ratio for the mean kSZ signal. This effect is especially marked at the largest scales, where the pairwise velocity distribution becomes more symmetric about zero. We show that splitting galaxies according to their local overdensity allows the convergence and divergence flows to be separated, yielding pairwise kSZ signals of opposing sign, with a reduction in variance for each subset. We use simulations to perform a detailed analysis of this phenomenon, comparing the cosmological information content in the global pairwise kSZ signal with our new density-split pairwise kSZ estimator. We consider galaxy catalogues comparable to datasets from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument, together with cosmic microwave background instrumental noise characteristic of recent and planned ground-based experiments. We predict that the density-split pairwise kSZ will increase the significance of detection by only a modest factor; nevertheless, we expect improvements by factors of respectively 11 and 4 in constraining $\sigma_8$ and $\Omega_{\rm m}$ when using the combination of Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument and Simons Observatory Large Aperture Telescope surveys.
item.dc:creator: Finn A. Roper, Aritra K. Gon, Yan-Chuan Cai, John A. Peacock

item.title: Optimal cosmological cross-correlation analysis with U-Net-based processing
item.description: arXiv:2610.30294v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cosmological cross-correlation analyses are commonly based on two-point statistics, which are optimal for Gaussian random fields but do not capture all relevant information in the presence of non-Gaussianity, which is ubiquitous in late-time cosmic fields. This motivates investigations of higher order statistics, and one method is to use machine learning to construct a correlation-optimized tracer field that can utilize cross-correlation information beyond two-point statistics. Using a tracer field as input and a paired target field as part of the cost function, we test whether a U-Net can learn a transformed tracer field that maximally correlates with the target field. We train a 1D U-Net on paired simulated fields and study controlled cases based on Gaussian and log-normal random fields. We train and quantify performance using the Pearson correlation coefficient with the target field and compare the network output with the analytic linear solution known in the Gaussian limit. For Gaussian fields, the U-Net reproduces the expected linear solution closely and behaves as an effective matched filter in frequency space. For log-normal fields, the network departs from the linear estimator and achieves an improved correlation with the target field, increasing the mean Pearson correlation from 0.857 for the linear estimator to 0.953 for the U-Net output. This indicates that the network is sensitive to information beyond the power spectrum. These controlled 1D experiments show that U-Net-based tracer transformation can effectively extract correlation-relevant information beyond the power spectrum, providing a promising framework for enhancing cosmological cross-correlation analyses.
item.dc:creator: Weitong Yan, Daniel Gr\"un, Oliver Friedrich, Andr\'as Kov\'acs

item.title: ULTRAMAN: A Proposed ultrasound detector for macroscopic dark matter
item.description: arXiv:2610.30507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose ULTRAMAN (ULTRAsound Macro ANalyzer), a passive ultrasound array experiment designed to search for macroscopic dark matter (macros) through coherent acoustic disturbances generated as compact objects traverse a controlled target medium. Unlike existing dark matter detectors that primarily rely on scintillation, ionization, or other signatures of energy deposition, ULTRAMAN exploits the acoustic response of matter to reconstruct individual highly supersonic trajectories using synchronized multielement ultrasound arrays. The framework connects macro stopping power and interaction cross section to the resulting acoustic pressure, while the expected event rate probes the macro mass and abundance. A genuine candidate would appear not as an isolated radio frequency spike, but as a correlated multichannel track consistent with a single highly supersonic passage through the target. Representative macro, nuclearite, axion quark nugget, and primordial black hole benchmarks are shown to occupy distinct regions of the resulting acoustic observable space. Existing ultrasound technology offers a realistic route to an event-level terrestrial search for macroscopic dark matter, with null observations translating into complementary constraints on its parameter space.
item.dc:creator: Oem Trivedi, Robert J. Scherrer, Alfredo Gurrola

item.title: Same Events, Weaker Bound: Model Dependence in Magellanic Microlensing Limits on Primordial Black Holes
item.description: arXiv:2610.30510v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: OGLE microlensing of the Magellanic Clouds sets the leading bounds on primordial black holes (PBHs) as dark matter from $10^{-8}$ to $10^{3}\,M_\odot$. Holding the detected events and survey efficiencies fixed, we show that changes to the Milky Way halo, the stellar lens populations and the Large Magellanic Cloud halo, each motivated by recent data, weaken the published strict 20-year bound by up to $\simeq6$, and by over an order of magnitude in an extreme stress test. With primordial clustering, the planetary-mass bound weakens by a factor $3.4$--$6$. We strongly recommend that compact-object dark matter limits be quoted together with their modeling assumptions and, generally, be derived under conservative assumptions.
item.dc:creator: David Morales-Zapien, Lucas Brown, Stefano Profumo

item.title: Constraints on interacting dark energy with a constant equation of state in light of DESI DR2: The role of the interaction term
item.description: arXiv:2610.30784v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent DESI baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) analyses suggest a preference for an evolving dark energy equation of state (EoS) that crosses the phantom divide $w=-1$. Interactions between dark energy and dark matter can also produce an apparent phantom-divide crossing in the effective dark energy EoS. In this work, we investigate interacting dark energy (IDE) models with a constant EoS parameter $w$, using cosmic microwave background (CMB) observations from Planck, ACT, and SPT, DESI DR2 BAO measurements, and type Ia supernova data from PantheonPlus, DES-Dovekie, and DESY5. We consider four typical forms of the interaction term $Q$. Our results show that the IDE models with $Q\propto\rho_{\rm de}$ generally exhibit a stronger preference for nonzero dark-sector interactions. In particular, for the CMB+DESI+DES-Dovekie data, the IDE model with $Q=\beta H_0\rho_{\rm de}$ yields $\beta=-2.52^{+0.80}_{-0.54}$ and $w=-1.510^{+0.170}_{-0.120}$, corresponding to deviations from $\beta=0$ and $w=-1$ at the $3.2\sigma$ and $3.0\sigma$ levels, respectively. Interestingly, the effective EoS of the IDE model with $Q=\beta H_0\rho_{\rm de}$ exhibits a redshift evolution resembling that of the $w_0w_a$CDM model, crossing the phantom divide. Bayesian evidence further indicates that this IDE model is favored over $\Lambda$CDM and the other three IDE models. Our analysis helps identify which interaction forms better account for current cosmological observations.
item.dc:creator: Zhao-Yu Li, Tian-Nuo Li, Guo-Hong Du, Sheng-Han Zhou, Yun-He Li, Jing-Fei Zhang, Xin Zhang

item.title: GPAge: a Global Parameterization based on cosmic Age for some unified early-time and late-time solutions to the Hubble tension
item.description: arXiv:2610.30961v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The over $5\sigma$ Hubble tension continues to motivate modifications of the standard $\Lambda $-cold-dark-matter ($\Lambda \rm CDM$) model. The large number of proposed resolutions for the Hubble tension, broadly divided into early- and late-time solutions, motivates phenomenological parametrizations to constrain the viable solution space. Recently, there is a growing interest in unifying early- and late-time solutions. In this work, we extend the original Parametrization based on cosmic Age (PAge) to cover both the early and late Universe. Specifically, we incorporate the radiation-dominated epoch at the background level and complete the perturbation sector within a unified-dark-fluid framework. The resulting parametrization can accurately reproduce target cosmological models at both the background and perturbation levels. Confronting this global PAge with cosmological observations, we find that it improves the best fit relative to $\Lambda \rm CDM$, but does not raise $H_0$ significantly enough to alleviate the Hubble tension. Our parametrizations indicate that varying the early-time matter-like density, even together with a flexible late-time expansion history, is insufficient to resolve the Hubble tension. These results suggest that resolving the Hubble tension requires pre-recombination physics beyond a simple retuning of the matter-like density.
item.dc:creator: Jia-Le Ling, Shao-Jiang Wang

item.title: Assessing the consistency of the CPL dark-energy model with cosmological data: Simulation-calibrated neural posterior disagreement
item.description: arXiv:2610.31044v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent DESI observations hint at a preference for dynamical dark energy with an equation of state that crosses the phantom divide within the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) parameterization. In this work, we assess the consistency of the CPL parameterization with current cosmological observations. We develop a model check based on the disagreement between posteriors inferred by neural posterior estimation and flow-matching posterior estimation. Both estimators are trained on the same CPL simulations, and their posterior disagreement is calibrated using independent simulations to obtain a global $p$-value. Controlled simulations assess the reliability of the calibrated \(p\)-values and show how detection sensitivity depends on the form of departure from the assumed model. Applying the test to the compressed CMB+DESI+DESY5 data vector yields $p_{\rm global}=0.524$, indicating that the current observations are consistent with the CPL model. The method has a median evaluation time of only $0.53\,{\rm s}$, enabling efficient assessments of cosmological model adequacy. This framework enables efficient tests of dark-energy models, providing a firmer basis for investigating the physical origin of cosmic acceleration.
item.dc:creator: Tian-Yang Sun, Tian-Nuo Li, Guo-Hong Du, He Wang, Jing-Fei Zhang, Xin Zhang

item.title: Cosmological Inference with Gravitational-Wave Dark Sirens and 21-cm Intensity Mapping: Forecasts for LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA with MeerKAT and SKAO
item.description: arXiv:2610.31081v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gravitational waves (GWs) and 21-cm intensity mapping (IM) are emerging as complementary cosmological probes: GWs provide direct luminosity-distance measurements, while neutral-hydrogen (HI) IM traces the matter distribution in redshift space. Their synergy offers a promising avenue for precise measurements of the Hubble constant. Within a standard-siren framework, we perform a joint cosmological and population analysis using $\mathcal{O}(150)$ mock GW detections with SNR > 12, as projected for one year of observations at LVK O5 sensitivity. We combine these with mock HI intensity maps from MeerKLASS and SKA-Mid, and study how observational limitations in both the GW and IM data affect the $H_0$ constraints. We find that uncertainty in GW parameter measurements is a dominant limitation on the cosmological constraints. Neglecting this uncertainty, the inclusion of HI information enables sub-percent constraints on $H_0$. We also find that observational effects in the HI surveys weaken the constraints, although they remain tighter than those obtained without HI information (spectral sirens). Despite accounting for HI IM observational limitations, including HI information reduces the $H_0$ uncertainty relative to the spectral-siren results by 61% for MeerKLASS and 53% for SKA-Mid. Because our results are based on a single realisation, they should be interpreted in light of possible realisation-to-realisation variability. Beam convolution most severely weakens the constraints. Instrumental noise can induce multimodality in the posterior, potentially biasing the inferred parameters. The results are sensitive to foreground under-cleaning and over-cleaning. Partial sky coverage has a relatively small impact. In the most realistic scenario, which accounts for both GW and HI IM limitations, we obtain $H_0$ precision estimates of 10% and 15% for MeerKLASS and SKA-Mid, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Dounia Nanadoumgar-Lacroze, Konstantin Leyde, Steven Cunnington, Tessa Baker, Ian Harrison, Ulyana Dupletsa, Simone Mastrogiovanni, Riccardo Murgia, Tommaso Ronconi, Matteo Schulz, Marta Spinelli

item.title: A cosmic filament catalog for COSMOS-Web Data Release 1 across 0.5 < z < 3.5
item.description: arXiv:2610.31168v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cosmic filaments represent the environments in which most galaxies form and evolve. However, the spatial distribution of filaments and the link between galaxy properties and their positions relative to filaments remains unclear, particularly at high redshifts. In this work, using the deep-field catalog COSMOS-Web Data Release 1, we construct a filament catalog spanning 0.5 < z < 3.5 that can be directly applied to studies of galaxy evolution and the galaxy--large-scale-structure connection at the peak epoch of galaxy and black hole formation. We developed a new procedure based on the DisPerSE method that fully incorporates the probability distribution functions (PDFs) of galaxy photometric redshifts by generating multiple realizations for each tomographic 2D slice. We then stacked these realizations to construct ``filament probability maps'' (w_ fil maps), from which filaments were subsequently extracted. The filament extraction parameters were optimized using mock catalogs generated from TNG simulations by minimizing the discrepancies between 3D and projected 2D filaments. Applying this procedure to the COSMOS-Web data, we detected 12,523 filaments (comprising 136,210 segments) across 0.5 < z < 3.5 and released a filament catalog, a companion segment catalog, and filament probability maps for each slice. Validation against astrophysical properties shows a strong agreement between the extracted filaments and those in the simulations, supporting the robustness of the filament extraction. These data products provide a robust foundation for investigating galaxy--environment coevolution at cosmic noon and beyond.
item.dc:creator: Qiaoyang Hao, Tao Wang, Weishan Zhu, Hong Guo, Peng Wang, Tiancheng Yang, Luwenjia Zhou

item.title: Robust paths to primordial $B$ modes in the presence of polarised point source contamination
item.description: arXiv:2610.31175v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A detection of primordial $B$ modes in the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) polarisation relies on a robust control and removal of contamination from astrophysical polarised foreground emission. We examine how much polarised extragalactic point sources may contaminate the cosmological signal in ground-based CMB experiments, propagating their impact through component separation to the final parameter constraints. We discuss masking and modelling strategies to ensure that the resulting constraints remain both accurate and precise under this source of contamination. We produce synthetic data containing polarised emission from extragalactic radio sources (ERSs) and dusty star-forming galaxies (DSFGs) following state-of-the-art models for both samples. We find that, while the DSFG contribution is likely too small to cause any significant bias to the cosmological or foreground parameters, the ERS contribution instead, if left unmasked, leads to a bias in the parameters describing the Galactic synchrotron and lensing $B$-mode components. For experiments targeting noise levels of order $\sigma_P\simeq 1\,\mu K\,{\rm arcmin}$, we find that masking all ERSs with fluxes above $\sim$0.1 Jy, coupled with a relatively simple model to marginalise over residual point-source contamination, achieves a suitable balance that allows for the robust recovery of unbiased cosmological and foreground parameters at a negligible cost in parameter uncertainties.
item.dc:creator: Arianna Rizzieri, Giorgia Zagatti, David Alonso

item.title: A cosmological intercept tension in local distance ladders
item.description: arXiv:2610.31181v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Hubble tension motivates direct tests of the internal consistency of the local distance ladder. We perform forward and backward consistency checks between Type Ia supernovae in Cepheid host galaxies and the Hubble-flow supernova sample using Pantheon+ data. Within flat $\Lambda$CDM, we impose Planck-CMB priors on one sample, infer the supernova absolute-magnitude calibration, and propagate it to the other sample to recover the Hubble constant, which should match the input value if the second and third rungs of the distance ladder align perfectly. We examine the impact of host-galaxy peculiar velocities using redshift corrections based on the Manticore-Local reconstruction. These corrections shift the recovered $H_0$ from $74.30^{+1.18}_{-1.20}$ to $71.37^{+1.23}_{-1.18}$ $\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}}$ in the forward analysis and from $60.83^{+0.98}_{-0.97}$ to $63.25^{+0.95}_{-0.93}$ $\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}}$ in the backward analysis, bringing both results closer to the input CMB constraint. Comparing the cosmological intercepts of the magnitude-redshift relation inferred from two rungs of the distance ladder before and after peculiar-velocity corrections, we find that the significance of the discrepancy decreases from $6.8\sigma$ to $3.9\sigma$ in the forward check and from $7.3\sigma$ to $4.3\sigma$ in the backward check. Peculiar-velocity corrections therefore partially alleviate the intercept tension, while a residual discrepancy persists within the adopted framework. Our results highlight the importance of local velocity modeling and motivate further tests of sample selection and calibration systematics in assessing distance-ladder consistency.
item.dc:creator: Haotian Dong, Marek Biesiada, Zhoujian Cao, Shao-Jiang Wang

item.title: Gravitational Wave Diffractive Images Reveal the Structure of Astrophysical Objects
item.description: arXiv:2610.31441v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scattering patterns encode the structure of extended objects, as demonstrated by charged particle scattering on atomic nuclei. Gravitational wave (GW) diffraction offers an analogous probe of otherwise invisible mass distributions. At linear order in the lens potential we derive expressions relating the central diffractive image contribution to a gravitationally lensed GW waveform to the Fourier transform of the projected lens density. For finite mass lenses this contribution takes the form of a point mass Born amplitude multiplied by a normalized mass form factor, analogous to that in nuclear scattering. As the frequency of GWs from a merging compact binary source evolves the signal samples this form factor across spatial scales, imprinting lens structure through interference with the primary image. Using full numerical wave optics calculations we quantify the observational reach for extended dark matter objects, primordial black holes halo-dressed by dark matter halos and superradiance clouds of ultralight bosons around black holes. For the considered source populations, five year observations with next generation detectors can distinguish extended lenses from point masses, probing dark matter fractions down to $\mathcal{O}(10^{-5})$, and halo-dressed primordial black holes from matched bare black holes, probing primordial black hole dark matter fractions down to $\mathcal{O}(10^{-6})$. For sufficiently close source-lens configurations, scalar superradiance clouds can produce distinguishable diffraction signatures for boson masses of approximately $10^{-17}-10^{-12}~\mathrm{eV}$. These results provide a framework for characterizing extended dark matter and compact object astrophysical environments.
item.dc:creator: Han Gil Choi, Sunghoon Jung, Volodymyr Takhistov

item.title: QUIJOTE scientific results - XII. Characterization of the polarized synchrotron emission at the power spectrum level in the QUIJOTE-MFI wide survey
item.description: arXiv:2610.31469v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an analysis of the polarized synchrotron emission at the power-spectrum level in the multipole range $30 < \ell < 130$, using the recent QUIJOTE-MFI wide survey (10-20GHz) in combination with Planck and WMAP data. The EE and BB power spectra are well described by a simple power-law model, with no evidence for the need of additional parameters. The best-fit slopes are $\alpha_{EE} = -3.24 \pm 0.12$ and $\alpha_{BB} = -3.81 \pm 0.34$ for $|b|>20^\circ$, hinting toward a steepening of the BB spectrum relative to EE at the $\sim 1.6\sigma$ level. The synchrotron frequency spectral indices are found to be $\beta_s^{EE} = -3.26 \pm 0.05$ and $\beta_s^{BB} = -3.25 \pm 0.10$ for the same cut, in agreement with earlier real-space analyses. We find no evidence for spatial variations of $\beta_s$ across different Galactic latitude cuts, within current uncertainties. The synchrotron BB/EE power ratio is approximately 0.2 over the considered multipole range, lower than typical values for thermal dust, and consistent with previous measurements. We also measure a dust-synchrotron spatial correlation in the range 0.1-0.25 over $30 < \ell < 130$. Using these results, we estimate the level of synchrotron contamination in future CMB B-mode measurements, finding an average power in the considered sky masks equivalent to $r \sim 0.003$ at 90GHz and $r \sim 0.0002$ at 150GHz for the relevant angular scales.

item.title: A Robust Estimator for the Lyman-$\alpha$ Forest 1D Power Spectrum at High Redshift
item.description: arXiv:2610.31626v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Lyman-$\alpha$ (Ly$\alpha$) forest flux power spectrum $P(k)$ is sensitive to a range of astrophysical and cosmological effects, including the thermal state of and large-scale fluctuations in the intergalactic medium and the nature of dark matter. Measuring $P(k)$ becomes increasingly challenging at high redshift, where fewer quasar spectra are available and higher Ly$\alpha$ optical depths result in lower transmitted flux. In addition, observational effects and missing data complicate standard Fourier-transform estimators. Here, we validate a likelihood-based estimator for $P(k)$. The method constructs the pixel-level covariance matrix of the transmitted flux field using precomputed $k$-space integrals that account for instrumental resolution and pixelization, enabling direct maximum-likelihood inference of $P(k)$. We test the estimator using mock Ly$\alpha$ forest spectra at $z \geq 5$, including analytic Gaussian realizations generated from known power spectra and forward-modeled simulation spectra incorporating observational effects relevant to high-redshift quasar surveys, such as finite spectral resolution, pixel sampling, noise, and missing data. We compare the recovered power spectra with both the input spectra and standard Fourier-transform estimates. We find that the likelihood-based estimator recovers the input power spectrum across the tested scales well within expected error and remains robust to the observational effects considered. This work establishes a framework for measuring Ly$\alpha$ forest clustering with a robust, nearly optimal power spectrum estimator, with particular focus on quantifying large-scale fluctuations that may arise from ultraviolet background fluctuations or the late stages of reionization.
item.dc:creator: Molly Wolfson, Joseph F. Hennawi, Frederick B. Davies, Zarija Luki\'{c}

item.title: Sound-Horizon-Agnostic Forecast for Constraints on $H_0$ and $\Sigma m_\nu$ from BAO, CMB Lensing, Supernovae and LSST-like Galaxy Lensing
item.description:
arXiv:2610.31660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a sound-horizon-agnostic forecast for constraints on the Hubble constant $H_0$ and the sum of the neutrino masses $\Sigma m_
u$ from a combination of LSST-like galaxy weak lensing, Simons-Observatory-like CMB lensing, the completed DESI BAO program, and expanded supernova samples. Treating the sound horizon at baryon drag $r_d$ as a free parameter, the method provides a consistency test of $\Lambda$CDM without relying on the standard early-Universe calibration of $r_d$. The analysis incorporates realistic galaxy weak-lensing systematics, explicitly marginalizing over photometric-redshift calibration, multiplicative shear biases, intrinsic alignments, and baryonic feedback, and extends the CMB-lensing analysis to $L_{\max}=5000$. For fixed $\Sigma m_
u$, we forecast uncertainties of $\sigma(H_0)\simeq 1.5$ km/s/Mpc with our least informative prior set, $\sigma(H_0)\simeq 1.3$ km/s/Mpc with more restrictive priors, and $\sigma(H_0)\simeq 0.7$ km/s/Mpc with an additional informative prior on the amplitude of primordial fluctuations $A_s$. Allowing $\Sigma m_
u$ to vary weakens the $H_0$ constraints, while still yielding a forecast 95% CL upper limit of about 0.4 eV on $\Sigma m_
u$. We also clarify the scope of the $r_d$-agnostic approach through validation tests using mock data from modified recombination and early dark energy models. The method recovers unbiased constraints on $H_0$ for the former but not the latter, highlighting its dependence on assumptions about early-Universe physics.
item.dc:creator: Seyed Hamidreza Mirpoorian, Helena Garc\'ia Escudero, Levon Pogosian, Amy Wayland, David Alonso

item.title: Partial geometrization of dark matter in metric $f(R)$ gravity: Exact reconstruction and growth constraints
item.description: arXiv:2610.30201v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We ask what fraction of dark matter can be accounted for by the geometry of a stable metric $f(R)$ theory, requiring the expansion history to be exactly equal to that of the $\Lambda$CDM model. Only a fraction $\xi$ of dark matter clusters as dust, whereas $f(R)$ supplies the rest, as well as $\Lambda$. We show that the background reconstruction reduces to a linear equation for $F\equiv f_R$, whose solution is $F-1=(1-\xi)\,\Theta(a)$, with $\Theta$ independent of $\xi$: the departure from general relativity is exactly proportional to the geometrized fraction. We solve this equation in closed form in the matter$+\Lambda$ and radiation$+$matter eras: in both, the solution is an elementary particular solution plus two hypergeometric modes. Stability requires $F$ to decrease monotonically in time, so $F$ cannot take its general-relativity value $F=1$ both at early and at late times. The effective gravitational coupling $G/F$ therefore necessarily runs: between the radiation era and the de Sitter attractor, $F$ changes by at least $0.837\,(1-\xi)$. In all stable reconstructions but one, $F-1$ grows as $R^{1/3}$ at high curvature, i.e., in dense environments such as the Sun, and local tests of gravity exclude them. The surviving member has $F\to1$ at early times: it recovers general relativity at high curvature and attains the minimal running of $F$. Keeping the linear growth factor at $k=0.1\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ within $10\%$ of its $\Lambda$CDM value requires $1-\xi\lesssim10^{-3}$, the weakest bound among all stable reconstructions; keeping $\sigma_8$ within $3\%$ requires $1-\xi\lesssim5\times10^{-5}$. Growth-rate data from DESI DR1 and SDSS DR16 give $1-\xi\lesssim10^{-3}$--$10^{-2}$, and the Cassini bound gives $1-\xi\lesssim10^{-10}$. A smoothly evolving metric $f(R)$ background can therefore geometrize only a negligible fraction of dark matter.
item.dc:creator: Davide Campanella Galanti, Oliver F. Piattella

item.title: Mass-Varying Dark Matter, Naturally
item.description: arXiv:2610.30253v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ultralight scalars that vary dark-matter masses require protection from quantum corrections. Cyclic $\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetries provide this protection but also suppress variation of the mean mass of equally populated partners. Unsuppressed variation typically requires asymmetric reheating through symmetry-breaking couplings that threaten radiative control. We show that scalar-induced mass splittings built into these constructions can instead bias relic abundances through symmetric interactions. The mechanism applies to thermal and nonthermal relics that reach internal equilibrium after production, and permits mass variation over a broad range of timescales.
item.dc:creator: C\'edric Delaunay, Seung J. Lee, Yuan Yin, Bingrong Yu

item.title: Variable-phase methods and data for long-range scattering
item.description: arXiv:2610.30261v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long-range interactions play an important role in dark-matter phenomenology, affecting the relic abundance, indirect-detection signals, and structure formation on galactic scales. Reliable predictions often require nonperturbative solutions of the Schr\"odinger equation over broad parameter ranges and many partial waves. We present a numerical framework based on the variable-phase method, which recasts the radial Schr\"odinger equation as a system of first-order equations and allows both regular and irregular solutions to be computed efficiently. The former determine phase shifts and Sommerfeld factors, while the latter provide additional information relevant for the self-consistent unitarization of contact-like inelastic interactions. We discuss the numerical implementation, integration-domain selection, partial-wave convergence, and comparisons with analytic limits. We release the code together with tables for the Yukawa potential containing phase shifts, Sommerfeld factors, elastic and angularly weighted cross sections, and the irregular-solution information relevant for unitarization. These resources facilitate dark-matter studies without requiring repeated computationally intensive scans.
item.dc:creator: Marcos M. Flores, Kalliopi Petraki, Thomas Pignard

item.title: The THESAN-ZOOM project: the delayed rise of Lyman continuum escape fractions in bursty high-redshift galaxies
item.description: arXiv:2610.30265v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The ionizing radiation that galaxies release into their surroundings depends on whether efficient Lyman continuum (LyC) escape coincides with strong photon production. Stellar feedback can open escape paths as the source population fades, linking the escaping radiation to a galaxy's recent history. We investigate this timing in thirteen high-redshift (z > 3) target haloes from the THESAN-ZOOM radiation-hydrodynamic simulations, post-processed with COLT radiative transfer and sampled at ~10 Myr intervals. The clearest delayed relationship links $\text{SFR}_{10}/\text{SFR}_{100}$ to the LyC escape fraction. Selecting the nearest positive cross-correlation peak gives typical lags of ~16 Myr and peak correlations of 0.4-0.6 in massive haloes, with longer and less coherent delays towards lower masses. The fitted delays scale approximately as $M_\star^{-0.19}$ and $M_\text{halo}^{-0.27}$, although the shortest lags approach the native snapshot spacing. Recurrent variations span multiple amplitude-dependent timescales, consistent with repeated episodes of star formation and feedback. Recent star formation closely tracks both intrinsic and escaping photon rates, while the escape fraction reflects the evolving gas transparency. The H$\alpha$-to-UV luminosity ratio retains a delayed association with escape, offering an observable connection between burst phase and leakage. High transparency during a fading phase can nevertheless yield little escaping radiation. The temporal overlap of photon production and transmission therefore shapes both the amount and timing of escaping radiation, informing the interpretation of observed leakers and their contribution to cosmic reionization.
item.dc:creator: Parth Mehrotra, Aaron Smith, Yuan Bian, William McClymont, Ewald Puchwein, Rahul Kannan, Laura Keating, Xuejian Shen, Mark Vogelsberger, Sandro Tacchella, Matthew Hayes, Crystal L. Martin, Cody Carr, Anand Utsav Kapoor, Shyam Menon, Alaina Henry

item.title: The black hole-galaxy correlations of the 12 micron local AGN sample: a NuSTAR perspective
item.description: arXiv:2610.30285v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The M-sigma correlation of inactive galaxies plays a crucial role in estimating the black hole mass (MBH) in active galactic nuclei (AGN): 1) it is used to calibrate the reverberation mapping (RM) method; 2) the RM is the basis of the single epoch method, the most-used technique to determine MBH of broad-line AGN; and 3) in narrow-line AGN, MBH is often directly inferred from the M-sigma correlation. The main goal of this work is to test whether the M-sigma relation calibrated from inactive galaxies can be reliably applied to a local AGN population spanning Seyfert 1, Seyfert 2, and hidden broad-line region galaxies (HBLRs), and whether the resulting AGN relation has sufficient predictive power to be used as an indirect MBH estimator. To investigate this hypothesis, we used the 12 micron AGN sample, a local representative and largely unbiased sample. Since a substantial fraction of this sample has good-quality NuSTAR data, we estimated their MBH with the X-ray scaling method, which works for any AGN accreting at moderate or high level. We find that the M-sigma correlation of the 12 micron AGN sample is different from the one obtained with inactive galaxies and has a substantial scatter. Therefore, its predictive power for MBH estimates is fairly limited. We also find that the MBH-Mgal correlation based on the 12 micron AGN sample is consistent with the analogous correlation obtained from a large sample of nearby type 1 AGN and inconsistent with that of inactive galaxies. Finally, we find suggestive evidence that Seyfert 1 and HBLRs have similar and systematically higher Eddington ratios than Seyfert 2 galaxies.
item.dc:creator: M. Gliozzi, L. Spinoglio, J. A. Fernandez-Ontiveros, M. A. Malkan, J. K. Williams, M. Young. A. D. Oxley, S. Satyapal

item.title: The PAU Survey: Active galactic nucleus galaxies in galaxy pairs
item.description: arXiv:2610.30309v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Aims. Leveraging the high-precision photometric redshifts of the Physics of the Accelerating Universe Survey (PAUS), we aim to investigate the connection between active galactic nuclei (AGNs) and galaxy pairs up to redshifts of $\sim1.0$. Methods. We identified 16,824 galaxy pairs with projected separations of $r_p < 100$ kpc and radial-velocity differences of $\Delta V < 3500$ km s$^{-1}$. AGNs were selected by cross-matching PAUS galaxies with multi-wavelength AGN catalogues, yielding 270 AGNs in pairs out of a parent sample of 8,880 AGNs in PAUS. We constructed control samples of isolated AGNs; non-AGNs in pairs; and isolated non-AGNs matched in redshift, absolute magnitude, and environment. Results. Active galactic nuclei in pairs show progressively redder rest-frame colours with increasing redshift, particularly at redshifts of $z\gtrsim 0.5$, whereas isolated AGNs and non-AGNs in pairs show no significant colour evolution and remain at $\mathrm{M_g-M_r}\sim0.65$. Pairs hosting AGNs are also preferentially morphologically disturbed interacting systems found at smaller projected separations and velocity offsets, consistent with more dynamically advanced interactions. Conclusions. These results provide evidence of a redshift-dependent link between galaxy interactions and AGN activity, suggesting that interactions play an increasingly important role in triggering nuclear activity at intermediate redshifts. This study highlights the unique capability of PAUS to probe AGN-galaxy interaction connections beyond the local Universe with unprecedented statistical power.
item.dc:creator: F. Duplancic, M. Siudek, D. Navarro-Giron\'es, E. J. Gonzalez, F. Rodriguez, S. Alonso, I. V. Daza-Perilla, D. G. Lambas, E. Gazta\~naga, A. L. O'Mill, M. Eriksen, J. Carretero, R. Casas, F. J. Castander, J. Garc\'ia-Bellido, H. Hildebrandt, M. Mezcua, R. Miquel, C. Padilla, P. Renard, E. S\'anchez, S. Serrano, I. Sevilla-Noarbe, P. Tallada-Cresp\'i

item.title: Gravitational Waves From an Entangled SO(3) Cosmic String Network
item.description: arXiv:2610.30360v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Discrete non-Abelian symmetries such as $\mathrm{A_4}$ are widely used in models of lepton flavor to explain neutrino mass hierarchy and their large mixing. If such a symmetry arises from the spontaneous breaking of a continuous group, cosmic strings can form. We study the breaking $\mathrm{SO}(3)\to \mathrm{A_4}$, for which the strings are classified by the non-Abelian group $\pi_1(\mathrm{SO}(3)/\mathrm{A_4})\cong \mathrm{T}'$, the binary tetrahedral group. Because the string fluxes do not commute, colliding strings may reconnect, pass through each other, or become joined by a bridge whose flux can belong to a different string network. We derive the probabilities of these outcomes directly from the group structure; in network models they are usually treated as free parameters. Including them in a multi-network velocity-dependent one-scale model, we find that the correlation length of the networks decreases and their energy density increases relative to Abelian $\mathrm{U}(1)$ strings of the same tension. The resulting stochastic gravitational-wave background is enhanced by up to nearly three orders of magnitude, showing that the algebraic structure of $\pi_1$ leaves a direct imprint on the gravitational-wave spectrum.
item.dc:creator: Mu-Chun Chen, Cameron Moffett-Smith

item.title: Decoherence of the quantum superradiant cloud from graviton emission
item.description: arXiv:2610.30723v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Black hole superradiance amplifies vacuum fluctuations into a macroscopic cloud of a massive bosonic field around a rotating black hole. Under free evolution, the quantum cloud is a two-mode squeezed state that remains entangled even at large occupation numbers, while its growing component admits a classical statistical description. In this work, we study how graviton emission changes the quantum state of the cloud. We find that graviton emission suppresses interference between cloud configurations with different amplitudes, but leaves interference between configurations that differ only by an overall sign unchanged. For typical configurations realized under vacuum fluctuations, the suppression becomes significant when the expected number of emitted gravitons is of order unity.We also show that, at larger occupation numbers, all first and second moments can be reproduced by a statistical mixture of coherent states. For the astrophysical black holes, both changes occur much before the spin-down of the black hole becomes significant.
item.dc:creator: Lingyun Fu, Hidetoshi Omiya, Takahiro Tanaka, Hui-Yu Zhu

item.title: Saxion Decay and Dark Radiation in the KSVZ Axion Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.31101v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We calculate the relativistic axion energy density produced by the decay of a curvature-displaced Peccei--Quinn condensate in a quartic KSVZ model. We follow the radial PQ field (the saxion) as it relaxes from its inflationary minimum and determine the surviving condensate abundance from the adiabatic action of its oscillations. We then evolve the condensate through its decay into axions and visible particles to calculate the resulting dark-radiation contribution, expressed as $\Delta N_{\rm eff}$. With one heavy coloured KSVZ fermion and no additional portal interactions included, the axion channel dominates the two tree-level decay modes. Two reference histories yield $\Delta N_{\rm eff}\simeq0.033$ and $0.12$, with maximum saxion energy fractions below $1\%$ and $4\%$, respectively. At fixed quartic coupling, increasing the duration of curvature release reduces the predicted axion radiation density relative to visible radiation by a factor of approximately $28$ while preserving the primordial isocurvature amplitude.
item.dc:creator: Sidhartha Samtani, Amartya Sengupta

item.title: Odd radio circle J1555+2726: Observational evidence for shock re-acceleration of fossil plasma
item.description: arXiv:2610.31664v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Context. Odd radio circles (ORCs) are peculiar extragalactic sources recently discovered. They are characterised by one or more bright rings extending on scales of hundreds of kiloparsecs, and are filled with fainter emission. A massive elliptical galaxy lies at the centre of ORCs. While their formation mechanism is debated, a shock is plausibly involved. Aims. We aim to constrain the nature of ORC J1555+2726 (ORC4) through the analysis of its morphological and spectral properties. Methods. We utilised Low Frequency ARray (LOFAR), upgraded Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (uGMRT), and MeerKAT radio data at 50-1284 MHz to obtain images and spectral index maps at high resolution and sensitivity. Results. Both the resolution and observing frequency affect the observed morphology. In particular, the brightness contrast between the ring and the filling emission becomes progressively smoother from higher to lower frequencies. We measured an integrated spectrum of slope $\alpha=1.06\pm 0.03$, a radio power of $P_{\rm 150}= (5.4\pm 0.5)\times 10^{25} \; {\rm W \; Hz^{-1}}$ at 150 MHz, and a radial spectral flattening down to $\alpha\sim0.5$ at the ring location. However, we inferred a negative (convex) spectral curvature and a peculiar spectral shape in radio colour-colour diagrams, which imply spectral flattening towards high frequencies. These properties cannot be explained by shock acceleration of thermal particles and standard ageing. Conclusions. The observed features suggest that a mixture of electrons with different spectra coexist within ORC4 volume, likely associated with shock re-acceleration of a fossil relativistic reservoir. The ring emission is plausibly dominated by higher-energy electrons re-accelerated at the shock front, while lower-energy re-accelerated electrons are more uniformly distributed across the whole source (possibly ellipsoidal) volume.
item.dc:creator: L. Bruno, B. Koribalski, R. P. Norris, A. Ivleva, T. Venturi, A. Botteon, C. J. Riseley, K. Dolag, J. R. Callingham, T. W. Shimwell

item.title: Understanding Big Bang Nucleosynthesis: the physics and its history
item.description: arXiv:2111.14254v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Big-bang nucleosynthesis (BBN) is a pillar of modern cosmology. It was the first major test of the hot big bang model, and today remains its earliest and most precise test. It all began with the trailblazing 1948 paper of Alpher, Bethe and Gamow, who proposed non-equilibrium nuclear processes in the early Universe and an early radiation-dominated phase to explain the abundances of all the chemical elements in the periodic table. While their neutron-capture model was deeply flawed, it initiated the path to the modern theory of BBN and the discovery of the cosmic microwave background (CMB). In this paper I clarify the basic physics of BBN, adding some new insights, and describe how the modern theory developed. I finish with a discussion of the pre-discovery predictions of the temperature of CMB, including the missteps and the missed opportunities. The legacy of big bang nucleosynthesis is enormous, and it is yet another illustration of how foggy it can be at the frontiers of discovery.
item.dc:creator: Michael S. Turner (KICP/UChicago,UCLA)

item.title: Vacuum Polarization, Geodesic Equation and Sachs-Wolfe Effect
item.description: arXiv:2502.08748v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the null geodesic equation for photons is modified in the presence of a charged scalar field, with quantum fluctuations acting as an effective mass term that changes the null paths to timelike curves. This effect can be interpreted as a vacuum polarization phenomenon in curved spacetime. The resulting contribution to the Sachs-Wolfe effect varies with photon frequency, leading to frequency-dependent corrections to the cosmic microwave background (CMB) blackbody spectrum in the form of a $\mu$-distortion, as well as modifications to the CMB power spectrum. We estimate these within a standard inflationary scenario and find that while the correction to the CMB power spectrum is significant when the scalar field is light, the magnitude of the $\mu$-distortion depends strongly on the regularization prescription.
item.dc:creator: Ali Kaya

item.title: Testing Bump in the Cosmological Power Spectrum Using Dwarf Galaxies
item.description: arXiv:2511.21134v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We analyze the possibility of using observational data on nearby dwarf galaxies -- their luminosity functions and spatial distributions -- to constrain deviations of the cosmological power spectrum from the standard one. Specifically, we consider a cosmological model with a "bump" in the power spectrum at a wavelength of 1.3~Mpc and a dimensionless amplitude $\mathcal{A}=2.0$. Such a spectrum is motivated by observations of an excess number of galaxies at high redshifts. The bump leads to a noticeable increase in the luminosity function in the range $-13 > M_B > -17$ at $z=0$. Comparison with observations constrains the bump amplitude to $\mathcal{A} < 0.25$ at a 3-sigma significance level for a wavelength of 1.3~Mpc. For wavelengths smaller than 0.8~Mpc, the bump manifests only in the luminosity function of dwarfs with $M_B > -14$.
item.dc:creator: Maxim Zabelkin, Sergey Drozdov, Oleg Skorikov, Sergey Pilipenko

item.title: Multi-tracers, multi-surveys: a joint Fisher analysis of DESI+PFS
item.description: arXiv:2604.25171v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Marginalizing over 11 effective-field-theory (EFT) nuisance parameters per tracer per redshift bin degrades cosmological precision in one-loop analyses of galaxy power-spectrum multipoles in redshift space. Simulation-based priors (SBP) tighten these parameters but rely on N-body simulations and halo-occupation-distribution (HOD) models. We consider a multi-tracer Fisher analysis as a complementary approach: auto- and cross-power spectra jointly constrain cosmology, galaxy bias and stochasticity through two channels -- within a survey and across overlapping surveys -- combined in a volume-partitioned joint Fisher analysis. We forecast across the $14{,}000\;\mathrm{deg}^2$ Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) footprint, including the $\sim\!1{,}200\;\mathrm{deg}^2$ Prime Focus Spectrograph (PFS) overlap at $z\in[0.6,1.6]$ with up to 4 tracers (PFS-ELG, DESI-ELG, DESI-LRG, DESI-QSO). We vary a common $\ln(10^{10}A_s)$, $M_{\nu}$ and ${\Omega}_m$, holding $h$, ${\omega}_b$ and $n_s$ fixed. Adding internal-DESI cross-spectra to DESI auto-spectra reduces the errors on the derived $f{\sigma}_8(z=1.1)$, $M_{\nu}$ and ${\Omega}_m$ by 7.1%, 3.5% and 3.8%, respectively, at $k_{\rm max}=0.20\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$. Adding PFS auto- and cross-spectra to this complete DESI multi-tracer analysis further tightens these errors by 3.8%, 2.6% and 3.2%, respectively, after marginalizing over residual cross-population stochasticity. The clustering likelihood alone constrains the linear and quadratic biases and the shot noise. For these parameters it provides a complementary test of inference using SBP, while the counterterms remain weakly constrained. The framework extends to any number of overlapping spectroscopic surveys.
item.dc:creator: Nhat-Minh Nguyen

item.title: Anisotropy and tracer-profile assumptions in aperture-based strong-lens dynamics: Conditional inference from supernova distance ratios and unresolved stellar kinematics
item.description: arXiv:2605.19615v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Single-aperture stellar kinematics jointly constrain the mass distribution, tracer light profile, and velocity anisotropy. Their coupling affects the interpretation of an inferred anisotropy. We quantify how tracer-profile assumptions and data treatment affect common-anisotropy comparisons and inferred mass-density slopes in a compiled galaxy-scale lens sample. We analyse 107 lenses using distinct \pantheon\ supernova counterparts, spatial flatness, distance duality, and the full supernova covariance. We compare the individual-slope power-law tracer with Hernquist and S\'ersic profiles using measured effective radii. Numerical Jeans solutions, likelihood comparisons, posterior distributions, and controlled recovery experiments quantify the effects of tracer representation. The power-law fixed-minus-free Bayesian information criterion differences are 6.74 for isotropy and 41.51 for fixed $\beta=0.18$, compared with $-3.89$ and $-2.26$ for Hernquist and $-4.67$ and $-4.30$ for S\'ersic $n=4$. The preference also changes with S\'ersic index. Removing 12 systems with linearised distance-ratio uncertainty above 20\% reduces the power-law isotropy comparison to 2.51. In isotropic S\'ersic $n=4$ and Hernquist simulations, power-law fits yield $\Delta\mathrm{BIC}_0>6$ in 60.0\% and 50.0\% of realisations, respectively, compared with 0.5\% and 1.0\% for matched-tracer fits.} {The preference for a common free anisotropy parameter depends on the tracer representation and sample composition. Controlled recovery identifies tracer mismatch as one mechanism that can generate this preference within the adopted aperture models. Physical interpretation requires joint treatment of photometry, distance uncertainties, and kinematic weighting.
item.dc:creator: Jian Hu, Yi Liu, Chen Wang, Jian-Ping Hu, Jia Zhao, Liangqing Zhu, Zhongmu Li

item.title: Fewer simulations, sharper covariances: Reducing mock covariance noise with Zeldovich approximation control variates
item.description: arXiv:2605.28817v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a control-variate method for reducing the variance of power spectrum covariance matrix estimates from simulations of large-scale structure. The idea is to pair each mock simulation with a cheap Zeldovich-approximation realization sharing the same initial conditions, and to use the known statistical properties of the Zeldovich field to remove correlated sample variance from the covariance estimator. Under a Gaussian disconnected approximation, we derive fully analytic expressions for both the optimal control-variate coefficient, $\beta(k,\ell;k',\ell')$, and the corresponding correlation, $\rho(k,\ell;k',\ell')$, in terms of the auto- and cross-power spectra of the target and control fields. In the monopole case, the correlation takes the simple form $\rho(k,k') = r^2(k),r^2(k')$, where $r(k)$ is the standard cross-correlation coefficient between the target and Zeldovich fields, implying that covariance estimation remains highly efficient whenever the two fields are strongly correlated. For masked redshift-space lognormal mocks, resembling LRGs from DESI, we find that the control-variate estimator reduces the variance of the covariance matrix by approximately an order of magnitude on large scales, $k\lesssim 0.05\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$, precisely where accurate covariance estimation is most challenging. The gains are smaller for higher $k$ but typically accelerate convergence by a factor of 2-3, substantially lowering the computational cost of covariance estimation for current and upcoming large-scale structure surveys. After a cheap parametric-bootstrap calibration of the precision-matrix bias, the control-variate covariance yields a $\chi^2$ distribution consistent with the expected number of degrees of freedom. This method is readily implementable in current imaging and spectroscopic surveys (e.g., DESI, \textit{Euclid}, LSST, PFS, \textit{SPHEREx}).
item.dc:creator: Boryana Hadzhiyska, Martin White

item.title: CMB Bounds on Primordial Black Holes via Radiation Capture
item.description: arXiv:2606.05133v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We explore the capture of neutrinos and photons in the cosmic neutrino and photon background by primordial black holes (PBHs). We model this phenomenon as a gravitational interaction that effectively modifies the continuity equations for radiation and PBH densities and the cosmic expansion history. We find that the observability of this modified cosmic history is highly sensitive to PBH mass, and only extraordinarily massive PBHs would leave observable trace on the temperature and E-mode polarization of the cosmic microwave background (CMB). Specifically, Planck data restrict PBH abundance to $f_{\rm pbh}\lesssim 10^{-1}$ for PBH masses above $10^{15} M_\odot$, getting considerably tighter for higher masses. We expect substantial improvement as high-resolution measurements of larger CMB multipoles become available. A future cosmic-variance-limited experiment, with $\ell_{\rm max}=7000$, would set $f_{\rm pbh}\lesssim 10^{-1}-8\times 10^{-5}$ (for the fiducial $\Lambda$CDM cosmology) across $10^{13}-10^{18}M_\odot$. These constraints would be comparable to the current limits at the high-mass end of the spectrum [Carr et al, 2026]. The gravitational interaction of PBHS with the cosmic background radiation and its imprints on CMB would thus provide an independent complementary probe of extraordinarily massive PBH abundance.
item.dc:creator: Marzieh Farhang, S. M. S. Movahed

item.title: Dark energy perturbations and the robustness of cosmological neutrino-mass constraints
item.description: arXiv:2606.28074v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Cosmological observations are placing increasingly stringent bounds on the sum of neutrino masses, approaching the lower limits implied by neutrino oscillation experiments. Recent studies have suggested that dynamical dark energy may alleviate this apparent tension. However, these conclusions generally rely on the assumption that dark energy remains smooth, neglecting its perturbations. In this work we investigate the robustness of cosmological neutrino-mass constraints by consistently incorporating dark-energy perturbations. Using CMB, BAO, RSD, and supernova data, we show that the commonly reported alleviation of the neutrino-mass tension in dynamical dark-energy models is not generic. While smooth dark energy substantially relaxes the neutrino-mass bounds, allowing dark energy to cluster shifts the preferred neutrino mass toward smaller, and even more negative, effective values. We demonstrate that this behavior originates from a degeneracy between neutrino free-streaming and dark-energy perturbations in structure-growth observables. Different combinations of neutrino mass and dark-energy clustering can provide similarly good fits to current data while yielding significantly different neutrino-mass constraints. Our results show that cosmological neutrino-mass measurements are inherently model dependent and that reliable neutrino-mass inference requires a consistent treatment of dark-energy perturbations.
item.dc:creator: Yu-Hang Yang, Emmanuel N. Saridakis, Yi-Fu Cai, Hao-Ran Yu

item.title: An E-value Reanalysis of DESI's Dynamical Dark Energy Signal
item.description: arXiv:2607.28918v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Cosmological surveys such as DESI release data in stages, and each release reprocesses earlier observations and supersedes its predecessor. Testing the same hypothesis at every release inflates the false-positive rate, and only the collaboration can estimate the cross-release covariance that an exact combination needs. We show how to combine evidence across such releases using public products alone. From each release we compute an e-value, a non-negative statistic with expectation at most one under the null, and we average these e-values with weights fixed in advance. Provided each release's own likelihood is correct, this average controls the false-positive rate at every release under arbitrary dependence between releases. For DESI BAO at a fixed Planck background, DR2 alone gives an e-value of $33.97$ against $\Lambda$CDM ($p \le 0.0295$) under our reference test specification, a flat prior on $(w_0, w_a)$ over a fixed box. The equal-weight average of DR1 and DR2 is $17.51$ ($p \le 0.0571$), below the rejection threshold of $20$. We did not fix these weights before DR2 was published, and the weights we now fix ahead of DR3 give $p \le 0.0874$ at DR2. Without a model of the cross-release covariance, an exact combination that counts each observation once can take any value. Under explicit models it ranges from below the threshold to nearly double the DR2 value, depending on the structure assumed. The evidence is concentrated in the LRG2 bin, which also changed most between releases. Without it the DR2 e-value falls to $0.49$, and a look-elsewhere correction over the seven redshift bins leaves no rejection. DR2 does not reject under wider priors either. The signal is therefore fragile and specification-dependent. We recommend that surveys report per-release e-values with a stated test specification and a combination rule fixed in advance, and publish the cross-release covariance.
item.dc:creator: Jinyoung Kim (Stanford University, Two Sigma Investments), David F. Mota (University of Oslo), Andrius Tamosiunas (University of Oslo, Case Western Reserve University)

item.title: The cosmic multipoles: a series of consistency tests for the Szekeres cosmological model
item.description: arXiv:2609.01154v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An important property of the quasi-spherical Szekeres cosmological model appears to be widely misunderstood in the literature. In this paper, the claim that the matter density can be fully decomposed on a given 2-shell into a dipole superposed on a monopole is shown to be inaccurate and exact propositions are substituted. Then, the multipole decompositions of three different quantities linked to the mass density are displayed and proposed to constrain the Szekeres parameters with observed data. A test of the axial symmetry assumption, together with that of an on-axis observer, using a property of the angular coefficients is also suggested.
item.dc:creator: Marie-No\"elle C\'el\'erier

item.title: Environmental dependence of galaxy properties in the southern GAMA regions
item.description: arXiv:2505.10429v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Using data from the Galaxy and Mass Assembly (GAMA) survey, we investigate how galaxy properties correlate with the local environment, focusing on the two southern regions of the survey (G02 and G23) that have not previously been examined in this context. We employ two-point and marked correlation functions to quantify the environmental dependence of galaxy color, stellar mass, luminosity across the $u$, $g$, $r$, $J$, and $K$ bands, as well as star formation rate (SFR) and specific star formation rate (sSFR). We also assess the impact of redshift incompleteness and cosmic variance on these clustering measurements. Our results show that $u-r$ and $g-r$ colors are most strongly correlated with local overdensity, followed by stellar mass. The sSFR exhibits a clear inverse relationship with density of the environment, consistent with the trend observed for $u$-band luminosity, which traces young stellar populations. In contrast, galaxies brighter in the $g$, $J$, and $K$ bands preferentially inhabit denser regions. By comparing our measurements from the southern regions with those from the equatorial regions of GAMA, we find that cosmic variance does not significantly influence our conclusions. However, redshift incompleteness affects the clustering measurements, as revealed through comparisons of subsets within the G02 region. The measured correlations provide key constraints for models of galaxy assembly across mass and environment, while the environmental trends in color and near-infrared luminosity offer a means to trace stellar mass growth and quenching with redshift.
item.dc:creator: Koti Joy, Unnikrishnan Sureshkumar, Anand Narayanan, Sabine Bellstedt, Anna Durkalec, Agnieszka Pollo, Matt Hilton

item.title: Crowdsourcing Gravitational Waves from Superradiant Axions
item.description: arXiv:2603.15734v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Black hole superradiance is a powerful probe of ultralight axions. If nature contains a boson with a mass of order $10^{-12}\,$eV, $\textit{mere vacuum fluctuations}$ will lead to its efficient production around spinning stellar mass black holes, forming a gravitational atom that both drains the black hole spin and decays to produce near-monochromatic gravitational waves. Existing superradiance constraints derive primarily from spin measurements of a handful of identified black holes. Here we instead present a detailed study of the population level effect: gravitational waves arising from both the 100 million black holes in the Milky Way and the stochastic signal from axion clouds throughout the universe. We study the impact of a broad range of systematic uncertainties on the black hole properties and compute the projected axion sensitivity for LIGO, as well as the future instruments Einstein Telescope, Cosmic Explorer, and a high-frequency Magnetic Weber Bar. We demonstrate that LIGO can robustly probe axion masses from roughly $10^{-13}\,$eV to $4 \times 10^{-12}\,$eV. If the black hole population extends to masses slightly below $5\,M_{\odot}$ - as hinted for by LIGO inspiral observations - LIGO would approach $10^{-11}\,$eV. Under that same assumption we show that a future high-frequency detector could push considerably higher, potentially beyond $10^{-10}\,$eV in the most optimistic scenarios, reaching towards the lowest masses within the projected sensitivity of axion dark matter searches.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian A. R. Ellis, Orion Ning, Nicholas L. Rodd, Jan Sch\"utte-Engel

item.title: Nested Sampling: A Critical and Comprehensive Theoretical Guide
item.description: arXiv:2606.17916v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The nested sampling (NS) technique has gained widespread attention, particularly in cosmology and astronomy, due to its ability to efficiently explore high-likelihood regions - a feature akin to an implicit likelihood optimization that underlies its success. While the full theoretical derivation of NS is complex and involves several approximations, the central challenge lies in sampling from the likelihood-constrained priors, which is crucial for its performance. This work provides a comprehensive and detailed exposition of NS derivation, clarifying both its theoretical foundations and practical challenges. We provide a thorough description of the NS procedure, emphasizing both its strengths and potential limitations. The connections between NS, importance sampling (IS), and vertical Monte Carlo are also discussed in detail. In doing so, this work seeks to deepen understanding of the method and to foster the development of future enhancements, novel variants, and more efficient implementations across a wide range of scientific applications. Thus, the main contribution of this work is twofold: it serves both as a tutorial for newcomers to the field and as a critical review for experienced practitioners.
item.dc:creator: Luca Martino, Fernando Llorente

item.title: Dark Energy and Neutrino Flavor from the Weak Axion
item.description: arXiv:2607.13128v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Dynamical dark energy offers an alternative to a cosmological constant with distinct observational signatures. However, the small energy density scale, Hubble-sized mass, and Planckian excursions make simple models fine-tuned and unnatural. In this work, we show that a weak version of the axion, identified with the phase field of the anomalous $U(1)_{B+L}$ of the Standard Model, can generate the scale hierarchies expected for dark energy. The axion potential is controlled by sources of explicit baryon and lepton number violation and is radiatively stable. We show that the leading contribution comes from two inequivalent Weinberg operators, one $B+L$-conserving and one $B+L$-violating, which generate the axion potential. We propose a flavor selection rule in the lepton sector that simultaneously removes the quadratic divergence and dominant temperature-dependent contributions to the effective potential. The resulting potential first appears at quartic order in the axion-dependent neutrino masses and, depending on the flavor model and PMNS parameters, its amplitude is parametrically close to the dark-energy density. Since the scale of dark energy is sensitive to changes in the neutrino parameters, improved measurements of $m_{\beta\beta}$, the sum of neutrino masses, $\delta_{\rm CP}$ and $\theta_{23}$ can favor certain models. Cosmologically, the field behaves as thawing quintessence, stays frozen by Hubble friction until late times and never enters the adiabatic regime.
item.dc:creator: Pedro Bittar, Carlos E. M. Wagner

item.title: Tighter Dark Matter Constraints from the Projected Mass Method: A Neural Network Enhanced Method for Galaxy Groups and Clusters
item.description: arXiv:2607.15339v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Measuring the total mass of the Milky Way and nearby galaxy groups is difficult because classical dynamical estimators rely on assumptions about satellite orbital geometry that are rarely satisfied in practice, and because only a handful of satellite galaxies are typically available as kinematic tracers. We present a new framework that corrects the well-known Projected Mass Estimator (PME) using a residual neural network trained on thousands of simulated galaxy groups from the IllustrisTNG cosmological simulation. Separate networks are trained for each satellite sample size, from as few as 5 satellites up to 50, so that the correction automatically accounts for the statistical noise that dominates when only a small number of tracers is available. In tests on simulated halos, the classical PME systematically overestimates halo masses by factors of $M_{\rm proj}/M_{\rm true} = 1.30^{+0.72}_{-0.62}$ (using the 2D distance) and $1.46^{+0.97}_{-0.72}$ (using the 3D distance), with RMSE of 0.29 and 0.32 dex respectively. The neural-network correction reduces this to $M_{\rm proj}/M_{\rm true} = 1.02^{+0.30}_{-0.26}$ with an RMSE of 0.13 dex. Applied to the Milky Way, the method yields a total mass of $M_{\rm MW} = 1.144^{+0.399}_{-0.296}\times10^{12}\,M_\odot$, with estimates based on the brightest 5-10 satellites favoring a somewhat lower range of $(0.8-0.95)\times10^{12}\,M_\odot$. The modified PME gives a tighter constraint on the virial masses and the inferred dark matter content of galaxy groups and clusters.
